dogecoin.text:
@cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @A_Burns__ @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay Because the payment method is, generally speaking, bad for the environment, bad for power grids, and it also lets the terrorists win.

If it were a safer method of taking donations, that'd be a different story, but most crypto really isn't fit for its own stated purpose.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay That last bit is a little unfair, given as the primary use of bitcoin at this point is to buy and sell bitcoin, whereas the primary use of the USD is to facilitate trade for millions of people worldwide.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay Nor should I.  As a self-interested actor I have absolutely no incentive to do anything whatsoever to legitimize your moon money in any way.  If anything, I have incentive to do the opposite, as does any other individual who isn't running a mining op.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay You acknowledge that inflation occurs, but you seem to think bitcoin solves this problem?  How?  Inflation is triggered by many things, but it is ultimately a function of time.  A currency with fixed max number of units isn't somehow immune to inflation.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay You say you look forward to regulation, but what would that even look like?  There's no actionable way to compel regulation here; that's why you guys like it in the first place.  Anything that could be put in place to regulate it would be nominal at best, which I think is known.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay And ultimately, for nonprofits I care about, I'd rather not see them get stung by something I think they're gonna get stung by, especially if I had a chance to say something.  
I've avoided the crypto conversation until now.  I don't want to participate in the Culture Wars.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay I don't like either of those outcomes, really.  But I'm a crypto nerd from before people only cared about it to make a buck off it.  In that capacity, I mistrust it.  I'm not convinced it's as bulletproof as the advocates want me to think it is, and they're sweaty about it.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay If you win, then there is a power upset and the dynamics of the world economy shift, and wealth inequality becomes more twisted in weird ways.  If everyone else 'wins', then traditional world superpowers continue holding the cards until megacorps finish devouring them.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay And that's ultimately the rub of it all.  You hold it all.  I don't hold any of it.  You and the holders need enough people to accept that it's valid and good, because then your time and energy are vindicated.  Everyone else needs the opposite for things to stay as they are.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay Everyone has equal access, but especially the people holding it all currently.  Ultimately, commerce depends on both sides agreeing that tender is valid, and philosophically and professionally, I just can't accept that your numbers are equivalent to the might of the US military.
@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay I'm not aware of any economies that aren't subject to corruption.  I'm interested to hear more here.

@A_Burns__ @cheesy_dad @XRPtheGoat7 @JasonDJudge @mozilla @dogecoin @BitPay Can you list some of the innovations bitcoin has led to?  I'd argue that your "in the red" doesn't solve the problems, but instead drives demand for solving the problems.  Big difference is the inertia between the two, but it's not the only one.  Thermodynamics for example.
